role: Visual Release QA / independent catalog reviewer
reviewScope: lighting-1 through lighting-12 exact current asset hashes

evidence.assetContinuity: PASS — GitHub compare 6b5401fcb708763b73525343ca82a172588ae0e0..8e49cff09f28c6cb4bfc44cba0f7d69d8e0dd7e9 contains no public/assets/catalog/lighting-*.svg changes
evidence.note: Actual branch-stored candidate bytes were rendered independently of canonical Store wiring at 240x210 card scale and 800x800 detail scale. Source/XML validity was not used as visual acceptance.

acceptanceBasis.familyFinding: All 12 Lighting candidates are recognizable, cleanly framed and materially different in object silhouette, but the rendered pixels use a shared flat-vector presentation: pastel gradient card, front-facing 2D/2.5D construction, white outline/glow, shallow material response and an embedded TIER badge inside the asset. Higher tiers add motif complexity and glow but do not reach the richer three-quarter dimensional toy-collectible materials, construction and lighting required by the screenshot target. The family therefore needs rework before canonical final-art promotion.

summary.nextAction: Repair lighting-1..12 in bounded versioned batches, prioritizing three-quarter dimensional construction, believable material/light response, stronger assigned-theme identity and removal of baked-in UI/tier chrome from the artwork. Preserve these reviewed hashes for comparison; every replacement needs fresh independent pixel review.

reviews.name: Starter Lamp
reviews.reason: Starter Lamp is immediately legible and unclipped, but the shade/base read as flat outlined vector shapes with minimal fabric/metal depth and no convincing three-quarter construction. Cloud Pop is directionally soft but the collectible target needs richer dimensional form lighting even at Tier 1; baked-in TIER 1 UI also belongs outside the art.

reviews.name: Cloud Lamp
reviews.reason: Cloud-and-raindrop lamp identity is strong at card scale, but the puffy body is essentially a flat white silhouette and Pixel Party is not materially expressed. Add dimensional diffuser/cloud volume, hardware depth and pixel-specific light/material detail; remove baked-in tier chrome.

reviews.name: Pixel Cube Light
reviews.reason: The stacked voxel/cube silhouette is distinctive and readable, but its faces remain flat polygons with little emitted-light or material depth; Berry Blast is mostly palette rather than themed construction. Give the cube convincing volume, emissive pixels and three-quarter collectible lighting without overcomplicating Tier 1.

reviews.name: Heart Lamp
reviews.reason: Heart lamp identity is clear, but the heart is a flat pink cutout on a stem and the Garden Glow assignment is not expressed beyond a pastel background. Tier 2 needs a believable glowing diffuser/material thickness, dimensional base/stem and botanical/garden-specific treatment rather than a UI-icon look.

reviews.name: Vine Light
reviews.reason: Arch/vine/bulb identity is distinct, but stems/leaves/bulbs render as thin flat vector pieces and Galaxy Glow is essentially absent. Rebuild with dimensional botanical structure, emissive bulbs, material highlights and a galaxy-specific light treatment while preserving the vine silhouette.

reviews.name: Planet Lamp
reviews.reason: Planet/ring/tripod composition and Sunny Pop palette read well, but the globe/ring are still flat luminous vector bands with limited glass/material response and spatial depth. Preserve this strong concept while giving the planet convincing volume, ring occlusion, tripod construction and premium directional lighting.

reviews.name: Sun Lamp
reviews.reason: Sunburst silhouette reads instantly, but the central disc/rays/stem are flat graphic elements and Aqua Wave is only a background color cue. Tier 3 should add sculpted radial construction, diffuser/material depth, more convincing emitted light and an aqua/wave-specific signature treatment.

reviews.name: Bubble Lamp
reviews.reason: Bubble-cluster identity is clear and distinct, but circles look like translucent UI bubbles rather than blown-glass globes; Art Attack is weakly represented. Improve refraction/specular depth, stem/base construction, spatial overlap and art-specific color/material storytelling for Tier 3.

reviews.name: Color Lamp
reviews.reason: Faceted prism silhouette and gold/purple Star Luxe direction are promising, but facets are flat polygon fills and the lamp lacks crystal refraction, edge thickness, believable mounting and richer emitted light. Elevate the same identity into a genuinely dimensional luxe crystal object.

reviews.name: Neon Strip Tower
reviews.reason: Midnight Neon theme and tower identity are the strongest in the set, but the tower remains a flat frontal panel with horizontal neon bars and no meaningful Tier-4 three-quarter chassis/material depth. Keep the palette/glow while adding premium housing construction, surface response, layered light spill and hero perspective.

reviews.name: Aurora Light
reviews.reason: Aurora arcs and candy palette read at card scale, but they are thick flat graphic strokes floating over a generic base. Tier 4 needs layered translucent/emissive light ribbons, dimensional support/base, depth/occlusion and materially richer candy-light treatment.

reviews.name: Crystal Chandelier
reviews.reason: Chandelier identity, hanging crystals and gold structure are readable, but the highest tier is still a front-facing line/shape composition with minimal crystal refraction, metal volume or chandelier depth; Adventure Club is only weakly conveyed. Tier 5 requires a much richer suspended 3D construction, luxe crystal/metal response and controlled spectacular lighting.
